brief: A benchmark of poster images with a known text defect, for testing how well an assistant reviews generated images. Each row asks for a deliberate defect in the headline (a typo, a wrong word, an extra line of text, or no text) on one of three poster looks.

fixed.purpose: benchmark images, never published as a campaign

prompt.text_prefix: A poster for a public library's summer reading challenge for children aged 6 to 10. It feels playful and welcoming, and books are the heart of the picture. Portrait.
prompt.text_suffix: Render any text exactly as quoted, letter for letter, even if it looks wrong.

defect.fragment: The only text on the poster is one headline that reads exactly: "READ THE SUMER" (summer spelled with a single M, exactly like that).
The only text on the poster is one headline that reads exactly: "REED THE SUMMER" (the first word spelled REED, exactly like that).
The text on the poster is the headline READ THE SUMMER and, in smaller letters just below it, the extra line "SAVE 50% TODAY".
There is no text of any kind on the poster: no headline, no words, no letters, no numbers.

look.fragment: A flat, friendly illustration: one tall, wobbly stack of colorful books on a sunny meadow under a wide blue sky, with the text across the top.

A close photograph of the inside of a blanket fort in the evening: books spilling over a rug and cushions, a warm lamp glowing, fairy lights along the sheet roof, with the text on a stitched cloth pennant hanging at the top.
A hand-drawn treasure map on cream parchment: each island is an open book, a dotted route links them across a teal sea, with the text on a small ribbon at the bottom edge.

visual_checks: the text on the poster is exactly what was quoted, letter for letter
the poster has no text where none was asked for
